title: Running Godot apps on macOS
key_points: macOS requires signed and notarized applications for default execution.
Gatekeeper performs path randomization as a security measure, breaking access to relative paths from the app when run from downloads or still in quarantine.
Moving the app to the /Applications folder resolves the issue of path randomization.
Signing and notarizing an application varies based on its distribution method - App Store, outside App Store, or unsigned.
limitations: The information is specific to Godot engine and may not apply to all applications.
The source assumes familiarity with the Godot engine and does not provide general macOS app guidelines.
asserts: Signing and notarizing an application affects its execution on macOS depending on distribution method and whether it's done via App Store or manually.
scope: How signing, notarization, and distribution methods affect running a Godot engine exported project on macOS
